displayPattern: Display on a GE touch-control dishwasher: a number followed by H, such as 1H, 2H or 3H (not all codes are found on all models)
meaning: Delay Start is on. GE says a number plus H, for example 1H, means the dishwasher is in Delay Start mode, and the number is the hours left before the wash cycle starts. It is not a fault. 1H starts with the number 1, not the letter I.
causes: The Delay Start or Delay Hours pad was pressed. Each press adds one hour of delay
A delay was set by accident while choosing a cycle
diySteps: To keep the delay, do nothing. GE says the control counts down the remaining hours and starts the programmed wash cycle at the end of the countdown
Opening or unlatching the door does not cancel the delay, according to GE
To cancel on models with a Delay Start pad, press that pad until the hours of delay indicator goes off
Models with a Delay Hours pad have no Off setting. Press and release Delay Hours until no number shows
On most models, GE says pressing and holding Start or Start/Reset for 3 seconds cancels any set cycle, including the delay. Then choose the cycle again and press Start
safetyNote: Switch the dishwasher off at its breaker before you reach into the base or remove a filter or cover, and let the tub and water cool after a cycle. Watch for sharp debris. Pump, heater, valve and control-board repairs belong to a qualified appliance technician.
proAdvice: A number plus H is a setting, so there is nothing to repair while it counts down. The delay range varies by model: GE's articles say most models delay up to 8 hours, some up to 12, and touch-control models range from 1 to 14 hours, so the owner's manual for your model has the exact range. If the display will not clear after canceling the delay and the dishwasher still will not start, GE's will-not-start article says a service call may be needed.
